annotations.text:
The phone is the design case: one hand, side of a court, evening light.

Every tap target is 44px or more. The bottom bar carries 22px of padding below its labels for the home indicator — env(safe-area-inset-bottom) in the build. Nothing the organizer has to read is below 13px.

All copy on these boards is lifted verbatim from copy.ts — no new strings were invented.

Desktop, without touching the phone.

The three tabs become a left rail; courts go two-up; standings sit alongside the round as a permanent aside. It is the same three destinations and the same signal-switched view — no router, no new screen.

Worth flagging: ADR-0016 words the navigation as "three tabs, bottom nav". Showing standings beside the round is what the handoff invites, but it is a change to that ADR, not just a stylesheet — probably an amendment rather than a silent divergence.

Dark is not a dimmed light theme.

The brand hue lightens (#0e6f87 → #3fa8c4) so a scoreline stays the brightest thing on a dark card, and brand-ink inverts to near-black. The podium keeps its own surface so it still reads as a block rather than a lighter row.

No in-app toggle — prefers-color-scheme only, per ADR-0018.

This is a proposal, not a settled identity.

ADR-0018 defers the visual identity until after a real padel night. Issue #25 is still open, so that night has not happened — treat every value here as a starting position to be tested at a court, not a decision.

Eight new tokens are proposed: podium-gold, podium-silver, podium-bronze, warning, warning-surface, danger, shadow-raised, shadow-sheet. The podium block is brand at 5% rather than a surface of its own, so the metals are the only warm colour on the screen. Adding them keeps the rule intact — a component still names only a utility (bg-podium, shadow-sheet), never a colour. The two shadows map to Tailwind’s --shadow-* namespace, so a card writes shadow-raised and no template ever spells out an rgba.

The body face is Verdana, chosen off the canvas: drawn for small sizes on screen, and installed everywhere, so the app carries no webfont for the text that matters. Only Space Grotesk loads from the network, and only titles and numbers depend on it.

Three ways the app could look. Every other page is built in A.

A was taken forward because the case to design for is a phone read at arm's length in fading light, and A is the one that stays legible without shouting. B is the most likeable in a clubhouse and the least readable outdoors. C is the most legible and the most opinionated — and it is a dark design whose light theme would always be the lesser half.

If B or C is the one you want, say so and it becomes the built-out set instead.
